paragraphs: Kedi. Rav Pappa said—and some say R. Shimi bar Ashi, and some say kedi—Bava Metzia (2, end of side a). Rav Adda objects—and some say kedi—Yoma (44a, 72b), Menaḥot (55b). Rava said—and some say kedi—Megillah (2b), Yevamot (90a), Nazir (2a), Ḥullin (73a, 81a, 118a). Rava said—and some say R. Yehoshua ben Levi, and some say kedi—Horayot (8, end of side a). This is not a sage's name, as they thought, but indicates that it was said without naming a sage, as in '(Pesaḥ) kedi nesavah,' Rosh HaShanah (5a); and Bava Metzia (27b), 'He mentioned identifying signs kedi'—meaning gratuitously. Likewise 'Did the eulogists eulogize in vain?' Ta'anit (5b). Therefore one should not write 've-kedi' in a bill of divorce, but 've-khadu.' Halikhot Olam writes likewise, citing 'Ulla said, and some say kedi,' in chapter HaRo'eh (I did not find this). Be'er Sheva, Horayot there, writes: 'In many places Rashi regularly explains that it is a Torah scholar's name' (I did not find this in Rashi); Be’er Sheva also reports another explanation: some transmit the statement without naming a speaker.
